To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) Mn and Cr form intimate metal contacts to Si with a barrier height of approximately=0.55 eV, and (2) these barrier heights do not change with time.

the barrier heights of the intimate metal-silicone contacts produced by Mn and by Cr on n-type silicon are approximately=0.5 eV, with no significant difference between them, that the barrier-height values do not change with time, and that there is no simple correlation between barrier heights and transition-metal work function.
(i) the barrier-height value does depend on transition-metal work functions, and (ii) it is not significantly affected by the presence of a thin oxide film at the metal-semiconductor interface.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of intimate metal-semiconductor contacts in which the metal is in direct physical contact with the semiconductor, and the barrier height is measured by both the I-V and the C-V methods.
the study of the electronic properties of intimate metal-semiconductor contacts.
the study of intimate metal-silicone contacts.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Schottky barriers produced by Mn or Cr on UHV-cleavage silicon are of high quality, with barrier heights of 0.53+ or - 0.02 e V and ideality factors close to unity.
the barrier height of the intimate transition-metal contacts is not determined by the transition-metal work functions, but by other factors.

there is a significant difference between the barrier heights of Mn and Cr contacts to n-type silicon, but this difference is not related to the work functions of these metals, and is not related either to their position in the 3d-series.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the intimate transition-metal-silicon contacts studied are not ideal Schottky diodes, and their barrier heights are determined by deep levels associated mainly with 'cleavage defects' and by the Fermi level pinching effect.
the barrier-height values of transition-metal-silicon contacts depend on the nature of the metal, the nature of the silicon surface and the nature of the defects associated with this surface.
the Schottky barriers produced by Mn and by Cr on UHV-cleavage silicon are of similar magnitude, and that the Fermi level pinns to a level approximately=0.5 eV above the valence-band edge.
The main takeaway from our work is that
intimate contacts to UHV-cleaned silicon can be obtained by evaporation of transition metals, and the barrier heights of such contacts can be measured with good precision.
the Schottky-barrier height for the Mn-silicon and Cr-silicon contacts is approximately=0.5 eV and is independent of the transition-metal work function.
the barrier heights for intimate metal-silicone contacts are independent of metal work function and are determined by defects associated with the cleavage process.
